finding: The anchor guard closes only the FINAL component of `bundle_root`. `O_NOFOLLOW` (Linux, l.1251) and `symlink_metadata` (fallback, l.1332) both leave INTERMEDIATE components unprotected, and for the workspace surfaces those are attacker-writable: `resolve_conversation_workspace_dir` accepts a multi-component `dir`, so root = `<ws>/<conv>/a/b` while bwrap bind-mounts `<ws>/<conv>` READ-WRITE at /home/sandboxuser (dispatch.rs:866). Swapping `a` re-anchors the whole kernel-confined resolution outside the workspace. Verified with a C repro against the real syscalls: after `mv proj proj.bak && ln -s / proj`, `open("<ws>/conv/proj/etc", O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY)` SUCCEEDS and `openat2(dirfd,"passwd",RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS)` returns the host /etc/passwd. For `run_from_workspace` this needs no race — the ephemeral row's `extracted_path` IS the live workspace dir (workflow_mcp/tools.rs:576), so a `kind: sandbox` step performs the swap deterministically between spawn_run's validation and a later llm step's `prompt_file:` read. The comment at l.1234-1244 asserts precisely this attack (`mv flow flowbak && ln -s / flow` → `prompt_file: "etc/passwd"`) is closed; it is closed only for a single-component `dir`.

The Linux/fallback equivalence claim for in-bundle symlinks is false. The comment says RESOLVE_BENEATH means 'a symlink that stays inside the bundle still resolves, exactly as the non-Linux fallback allows, while one that leaves it fails with EXDEV'. Measured on a real kernel: an ABSOLUTE symlink inside the bundle pointing at a file inside the bundle returns EXDEV (RESOLVE_BENEATH rejects all absolute symlinks by definition), as does a relative symlink whose target climbs out and back (`../b/sub/real.md`) — while `open_confined_fallback`'s canonicalize+starts_with ACCEPTS and reads both. So the same bundle is a security `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE` on Linux and valid on macOS/Windows/pre-5.6, and a legitimate in-bundle absolute symlink (`ln -s $PWD/prompts/task.md p.md`, trivially produced in the sandbox workspace or by a tarball) gets a false security verdict. This is the same class the O_NOFOLLOW removal was meant to fix, moved one level down.

`validate_from_workspace` is an `async fn` and still calls the SYNC `validate_collecting(&def, &root, false)` on a REAL bundle root — the conversation's sandbox workspace, which the model writes. That performs the blocking `std::fs` open+fstat+read of every distinct `prompt_file:` (up to MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES = 1 MiB each) directly on the tokio worker handling the JSON-RPC request. This is exactly the defect `validate_for_install_async` was introduced to fix; the sibling verb `load_and_validate_workspace` (l.542) was converted in this diff and this one was missed. A model can also park the worker on a slow/hung FS object here since the read is unbounded in time.

`validate_for_install_async`'s doc comment states a falsehood the code contradicts: 'EVERY caller holding a real bundle goes through here — ... and `workflow_mcp`'s workspace verbs, which carry the largest such root of all (the conversation's sandbox workspace). The only callers left on the sync form are the DRAFT-validation handlers, which pass a bundle root that does not exist and therefore read nothing at all.' `workflow_mcp/tools.rs:686` (`validate_from_workspace`) is a workspace verb on the sync form with a real, existing, model-written root. The comment is the reason the miss is invisible.

TEST-14's doc claims 'the property is asserted for BOTH resolution paths ... so cfg-disabling `openat2` leaves this green while REMOVING either anchor guard turns it red.' Verified false by experiment: deleting the fallback's `symlink_metadata`+`is_dir` anchor guard (l.1332-1338) leaves `read_prompt_file_refuses_a_bundle_root_that_became_a_symlink` and the whole workflow suite GREEN on Linux (the only platform CI runs), because openat2 is taken. The fallback's anchor guard — the sole anchor protection on macOS/Windows/pre-5.6 kernels — has no test that can fail on the test platform. Separately verified: forcing `open_confined` to call `open_confined_fallback` on Linux keeps all 56 workflow::validate/workflow::dispatch tests green, so NO test distinguishes the two resolution paths.

`ELOOP` is folded into `PromptFileError::Escape` → the SECURITY finding `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE` whose message is "resolves outside bundle". Measured: an ordinary symlink LOOP entirely inside the bundle (`a -> b`, `b -> a`) returns ELOOP from openat2, so it is reported as a confinement escape it is not. The fallback reports the identical bundle as `Unreadable` → the SEMANTIC `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING` (canonicalize returns ELOOP). Wrong layer on Linux and a second Linux/fallback verdict divergence.

openat2's documented `EAGAIN` ('the kernel detected a racing rename/mount while enforcing RESOLVE_BENEATH; the caller should retry') is unhandled — it falls into the `_` arm and becomes `Unreadable("Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)")` → `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING`. There is no retry, so ordinary concurrent activity in the (model-writable) workspace can nondeterministically fail a legitimate prompt file, and the author-facing copy blames their file. Since the errno arms were rewritten in this diff, and EAGAIN is specific to the RESOLVE_BENEATH the diff introduced, it is a gap of this change.

A `rel` containing a NUL byte diverges between the two paths: on Linux `CString::new(rel)` fails → `PromptFileError::Unsafe` → security `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE`; on the fallback `canonicalize` returns InvalidInput → `Unreadable` → semantic `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING`. `check_prompt_file_shape` (the one place that is supposed to own the platform-independent shape verdict) does not reject NUL, so the verdict is decided by whichever resolver happens to run.

The `#[cfg(not(unix))] { std::fs::File::open(root) }` arm of the anchor open is unreachable by construction: it sits inside `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] fn open_confined`, and Linux always satisfies `unix`. It also silently documents a symlink-FOLLOWING anchor open as an acceptable alternative to the O_NOFOLLOW one directly above it.

Two pre-existing test comments now describe code this diff deleted. `prompt_file_missing_in_bundle_is_reported` says the MISSING verdict happens because '(canonicalize fails)', and `prompt_file_escaping_bundle_via_symlink_is_reported` (l.2625) says the ESCAPE verdict 'trips the post-canonicalize confinement guard'. The canonicalize+starts_with sequence they name was removed from `check_prompt_files`; on the platform these tests run (Linux) the verdicts now come from openat2 ENOENT/EXDEV.

The per-distinct-path read dedup (`seen` HashMap) — the prior round's named fix for per-step read amplification — has no test: deleting the cache and reading per step changes no assertion, so the amplification can silently return. The same holds for the `Vec::with_capacity(meta.len().min(MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES))` clamp (l.1473) and for `validate_for_install_async`'s `spawn_blocking` (l.596); the test module is otherwise explicit about which guards it cannot falsify, and these three are not among the ones it names.

`read_prompt_file`'s doc asserts unconditionally that 'the validator cannot pass something the runner then fails on'. `check_prompt_files` skips the whole existence half when `!bundle_root.is_dir()` (l.1555), and `spawn_run`/`resume_run` use that same code path against `workflow.extracted_path`. If a bundle dir is missing (orphaned install, deleted workspace), validation reports no prompt-file finding and the run then fails in `load_raw_prompt`. The doc frames the skip as a DRAFT-surface concession; it applies to the real launch path too.

REJECTED: the `ENOSYS | EPERM -> open_confined_fallback` arm silently downgrades to the weaker resolver on a per-call basis, which would matter if an attacker could induce EPERM. Investigated openat2(2)'s EPERM conditions for an `O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC` open with RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS; no attacker-inducible case found (EPERM there is O_NOATIME- or seccomp-shaped, both deployment properties). Not a hole.

REJECTED: unbounded allocation / unbounded read in `read_prompt_file`. The capacity hint is clamped to MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES, the read is `Read::take(MAX+1)`, and the post-read length is re-checked, so peak allocation is ~1 MiB + 1 byte regardless of what fstat claims or how the file grows mid-read. `String::from_utf8` reuses the buffer. Sound.

REJECTED: unsoundness in the two `unsafe` blocks. `mem::zeroed::<libc::open_how>()` is valid (repr(C) integers only, and openat2(2) requires unknown fields to be zero); `libc::syscall(SYS_openat2, ...)` is passed a live owned dirfd, a NUL-terminated CString whose lifetime outlives the call, a fully-initialised `open_how` and an explicit size; `File::from_raw_fd(fd as RawFd)` takes ownership of a fresh descriptor exactly once and the `fd < 0` case returns before it. The i64->i32 narrowing cannot lose bits for a valid fd. No leak: `dir` drops at end of scope, and std forces O_CLOEXEC on both `OpenOptions` opens.
